correctness.rationale: Eq. (2.5) explicitly specifies a spherical projection-only observation, whereas Eqs. (2.6)–(2.8) and the posterior use two full-space independent Gaussian transitions centered successively on X=G eta+B xi and r. With xi~N(0,I) and G,B orthonormal complementary, the actual conditional covariance of Z given eta is sI+BB^T, with distinct eigenvalues s and s+1. Projection B^T Z is xi plus independent N(0,sI), giving cross-covariance I and exact mutual information (n-K)/2 log(1+1/s). Integrating auxiliary r from the joint likelihood while holding X fixed gives phi_n(Z;X,sI); survival depends only on X and fixed other parameters, so variance allocations of fixed s are observationally indistinguishable. The three-dimensional replay checks matrices, Gaussian densities and numerical mutual information. The proof covers all n,K and positive variances.

value.rationale: The source advertises latent-component recovery without external validation and a separation of process loss from measurement noise as central theoretical contributions. The exact observation-law theorem shows that the fitted likelihood does not actually suppress the nominally hidden orthogonal channel and that distinct precision parameters in its Gibbs sampler correspond to an unchanged observed-data likelihood whenever the variances have equal sum. This changes model interpretation, experimental identifiability, and the meaning of posterior uncertainty decomposition; a different measurement kernel or extra validation information is needed to address it. These are substantive reliability-model design limits, not mere normalization or sign typos.
